annotation.organism: Thermus thermophilus (strain ATCC BAA-163 / DSM 7039 / HB27)
function: Catalyzes the last step of the phosphorylated serine biosynthetic pathway, i.e. dephosphorylation of O-phospho-L-serine to form L-serine. Is also able to dephosphorylate O-phospho-D-serine with similar efficiency. Displays a poor activity on L-phosphothreonine, and cannot use L-phosphotyrosine, pyridoxal phosphate, glucose 6-phosphate, or fructose 6-phosphate as substrates.

annotation_comments.text: Cells lacking this gene cannot grow in minimal medium, in contrast to wild type. ysaA, serA, and serC deletion mutants have virtually identical profiles when observed across all the conditions studied, likely placing YsaA in the serine biosynthesis pathway. The defect is complemented by glycine, or a combination of serine and other amino acids such as glutamine or glutamate. The inability of serine alone to rescue the growth defect of the deletion mutant is due to serine toxicity.
